drivingQuestion: How many unfinished steps may remain when setting a price?

segments.he: הָיָה הוּא תְּחִלָּה לַקּוֹצְרִים. אָמַר רַב: מְחוּסָּר שְׁתַּיִם – פּוֹסֵק. שָׁלֹשׁ – אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק. וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בִּידֵי אָדָם – אֲפִילּוּ מֵאָה פּוֹסֵק. בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם – אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵק.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if the seller «was first among the reapers,» he may set a price with the buyer only when the produce he has is ready for delivery. «Rav says:» If only «two» actions needed to complete the labor to prepare the produce were «lacking, he may set» a price, as the produce is viewed as if it had already been prepared. But if «three» actions were lacking, «he may not set» a price, as the item is still not considered prepared, and the setting of a price in advance creates a concern of interest. «And Shmuel says:» If the actions needed to complete the labor are to be performed «by human hands,» then «even» if «one hundred» actions were lacking, «he may set» a price, but if the necessary actions must be accomplished «by the hand of Heaven,» then «even» if «one» action is lacking, «he may not set» a price.
